# Matches of leak-patterns.txt that are not leaks. Perl-compatible regular expressions, one per
# line; an entry must match the whole matched text. Keep entries narrow: prefer changing the
# source (an RFC 5737 address, a neutral name) to adding one here.

# Unspecified, loopback, private (RFC 1918) and documentation (RFC 5737) IPv4 addresses.
0\.0\.0\.0
127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+
10\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+
172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.\d+\.\d+
192\.168\.\d+\.\d+
192\.0\.2\.\d+
198\.51\.100\.\d+
203\.0\.113\.\d+

# Link-local (RFC 3927) and shared CGNAT (RFC 6598) IPv4 ranges: never routable on the internet,
# used by the SSRF-guard tests as addresses the guard must refuse.
169\.254\.\d+\.\d+
100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\.\d+\.\d+

# Other IANA special-purpose IPv4 ranges (RFC 6890) that SSRF guards refuse: IETF protocol
# assignments, the 6to4 relay anycast, benchmarking, multicast, and reserved space up to broadcast.
192\.0\.0\.\d+
192\.88\.99\.\d+
198\.1[89]\.\d+\.\d+
(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+
(24[0-9]|25[0-5])\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+
